text:
To: Site Supervisors
From: Hadley Finch, Construction Director
Subject: Weather contingency

The forecast for the coming fortnight predicts heavy rain, and work on the Brinton Road project is likely to be disrupted. [1] Supervisors should therefore review the schedule for external tasks, in particular the pouring of concrete, which cannot proceed in wet conditions.

Where work has to be suspended, the supervisor must [2] the delay in the site diary, together with the reason and the time lost. These records are essential [3] the client may be entitled to an extension of the completion date. [4] the programme is already tight, I would ask you to identify tasks that can be carried out under cover so that idle time is kept to a minimum.

choices: Delays caused by weather are a recognized ground for adjusting the contract period, provided that they are properly documented.
Delays caused by weather are an unrecognized ground for adjusting the contract period, whether or not they are documented.
Delays caused by suppliers are a recognized ground for adjusting the contract period, provided that they are properly invoiced.
Weather caused by delays is a recognized ground for documenting the contract period, provided that it is adjusted.
questions.explanation: The next sentence tells supervisors to review the schedule 'therefore', so the previous one must make the weather problem a consequential contractual matter; only the first does.
One 'logs' a delay in the site diary, meaning records it; 'lodge' means submit or stay, 'lock' and 'loom' do not fit.
'Because the client may be entitled' gives the reason the records are essential; 'unless' and 'whereas' do not.
'Since the programme is already tight' gives the reason for the request; the others do not.

text:
BUILDING MANAGEMENT NOTICE

All tenants are reminded that the fire alarm system will be tested on the first Monday of every month at 10 a.m. [1] The test will last approximately ten minutes, during which the alarm will sound continuously. Tenants are not required to leave the building, [2] they should not assume that the alarm indicates a test unless an announcement is made to that effect.

If an alarm sounds at any other time, it must be treated as genuine, and everyone should proceed immediately to the nearest exit. Lifts will not be [3] during an evacuation. Anyone who needs assistance to leave the building should register with the front desk, so that arrangements can be made [4] advance.

choices: The date of each test is fixed in advance, and the building manager will confirm it by e-mail on the preceding Friday.
The date of each test is chosen at random, and the building manager will confirm it by e-mail on the following Friday.
The date of each test was fixed in advance, and the building manager confirmed it by e-mail on the preceding Friday.
The date of each tenant is fixed in advance, and the test manager will confirm it by e-mail on the preceding Friday.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes the test and its duration, so the previous one should give the schedule; only the first is coherent and uses the correct tense.
'Although' concedes that tenants need not leave yet warns them not to assume it is a test; the others invert the logic.
'Lifts will not be available' needs the adjective; the other forms are not grammatical after 'be'.
